verses.1: After saying these words, Jesus went away with his disciples across the winter snowy region of Cedar. There was a cave where he and his disciples entered.
verses.2: Also, Judas knew the location well, as Jesus often spent time there with his disciples.
verses.3: So Judas, taking the spear, along with the help of the high priests and the Pharisees, arrived there, accompanied by torches, lights, and weapons.
verses.4: Jesus, knowing all that would happen to him, went out and said to them, “What do you seek?”
verses.5: They replied to him, “Yes, I am Jesus of Nazareth.” He said to them, “I am who you are looking for.” Then Judas also stood there, who had betrayed him along with them.
verses.6: So he said to them, “I am it. Let us go back, and fall down.”
verses.7: Once again, he asked them, “Who do you seek?” They replied, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
verses.8: Jesus replied, “I tell you that I am. If you seek me, then go and bring these people here.”
verses.9: So that the words he said might be fulfilled: “For whom you give, I will not take away anything from them.”
verses.10: Simon Peter, therefore, took a sword and attacked her. He also humiliated the priest’s servant, cutting off his right ear. The name of that servant was Malchus.
verses.11: Then Jesus said to Peter, “Put the sword into the scabbard. Isn’t the cup that my Father has given me not to drink?”
verses.12: So, the governor and the Jewish officials also captured Jesus and took him away.
verses.13: And they first brought him before Hanna. For Kiafa was a man who was very sad; he was the high priest of that dynasty.
verses.14: And Kaifas was the one who advised the Jews that it was better for one person to die than for the entire people to perish.
verses.15: Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. That disciple was known to the high priest, so he went into the high priest’s courtyard with Jesus.
verses.16: And Peter stood outside the door. Then the other disciple, who knew the high priest, went out and said to the doorkeeper, and he brought Peter inside.
verses.17: So, the disciple says to Peter, “You too are not one of these men.” He replies, “I am not.”
verses.18: The slaves and servants also became covered in coal, thinking that it was fire. They continued to heat themselves up. Peter was also among them, and he too kept heating himself up.
verses.19: So, the high priest asked Jesus about his disciples and his way of teaching.
verses.20: Jesus said to him, “I have spoken to the world. I have always taught in gatherings and in the temple, where all the Jews gather. But in secret, I never spoke anything.”
verses.21: What do you want to know? Ask those who listened to me what I said. See, they know exactly what I said.
verses.22: When he said these things, one of the servants stood up and gave Jesus a towel, saying, “May I do this for you?” Should he respond to the high priest in such a manner?
verses.23: Jesus replied to him, “If I have spoken wrongly, prove it by your own words. But if I have spoken rightly, why do you accuse me?”
verses.24: So, Hanna sent him away, tied up and ready to be given to the high priest, Caiaphas.
verses.25: And Simon Peter was also there, and he was getting hot from the heat. I said to him, “Aren’t you among his disciples too?” He denied it and said, “No, I am not.”
verses.26: One of the priest’s servants said, “I’m a relative of that man who cut off Peter’s ear. Have I not seen you in the garden with him?”
verses.27: Once again, Peter refused. And immediately, he cried out in anger.
verses.28: They therefore took Jesus away from Caiaphas to the court where he would be judged. It was still early in the day. They did not go into the court right away, so that they wouldn’t be tempted to eat during the time of fasting.
verses.29: So, Pilate came out to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
verses.30: They also said to him, “If he wasn’t a person who does evil deeds, then we wouldn’t have given him over to you.”
verses.31: So Pilate said to them, “Take him away. Judge him according to your own laws.” The Jews said to him, “It is not right for us to kill anyone.”
verses.32: So that the words of Jesus could be fulfilled, meaning that he was about to die.
verses.33: So, Pilate once again entered the court and greeted Jesus. He said to Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?”
verses.34: Jesus replied, “Do you say this because of yourself, or do others tell you about me?”
verses.35: Pilatus said, “Am I a Jew? Your people and the high priests have given me this position. What have I done?”
verses.36: Jesus said, “My kingdom isn’t of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would fight that I should not give my throne to the Jews. But now, my kingdom isn’t of this world.”
verses.37: Then Pilate said to him, “Are you the king?” Jesus replied, “You say that I am the king. I was born for this purpose, and I came into the world to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who hears the voice of truth will listen to me.”
verses.38: Pilato said to him, “What is the truth?” After saying this, he went back to the Jews and said to them, “I find no fault in him at all.”
verses.39: It’s customary for me to dismiss one of you during the festival. So, please allow me to dismiss the king of the Jews as well.
verses.40: They cried out again, saying, “Not this one, but Barabbas instead.” And Barabbas was a traitor.
